record.context_brief: fundamental groups of compact complete affine flat manifolds
record.original_question: Milnor's theorem implies that the fundamental group of a complete affine flat manifold is virtually polycyclic and torsion free, and conversely every virtually polycyclic group occurs as the fundamental group of some complete affine flat manifold. Which groups can occur as the fundamental group of a compact complete affine flat manifold?

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.8. The fundamental group of a complete affine flat manifold is virtually polycyclic and torsion free. Conversely, for any virtually polycyclic group G, there exists a complete affine flat manifold M such that π_1(M)=G.
Question 2.9. Which virtual group could be the fundamental group of a compact complete affine flat manifold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An affine flat manifold is a smooth manifold M equipped with a flat torsion-free affine connection; equivalently, M admits an atlas whose transition maps are restrictions of affine transformations of R^n. Such a manifold is called complete if its universal cover, with the lifted affine structure, is affinely isomorphic to R^n; equivalently, the developing map is a diffeomorphism onto R^n. In this case the fundamental group π_1(M) acts properly discontinuously and freely on R^n by affine transformations, so M = R^n / Γ for a torsion-free discrete subgroup Γ of the affine group Aff(R^n) = GL(n,R) ⋉ R^n.

It is known that for any complete affine flat manifold M (not necessarily compact), the group π_1(M) is virtually polycyclic and torsion-free, and conversely every torsion-free virtually polycyclic group arises as π_1(M) for some complete affine flat manifold M.

Problem. Characterize precisely the class of groups Γ that occur as the fundamental group of some compact complete affine flat manifold. That is, determine which torsion-free virtually polycyclic groups Γ admit a properly discontinuous, free, cocompact action on R^n by affine transformations for some n.
artifact.category_tag: Affine flat manifolds and Auslander conjecture
artifact.status_search_result: The question is closely tied to Auslander's conjecture (1964), which asserts that the fundamental group of every compact complete affine flat manifold is virtually polycyclic (equivalently virtually solvable in this setting). The conjecture is known in low dimensions: proven in dimension 3 by Fried–Goldman, and established up to dimension 6 by Abels–Margulis–Soifer, as well as in cases where the holonomy preserves a Lorentz metric. It remains open in general for dimensions ≥ 7. A complete characterization of which virtually polycyclic groups arise is therefore not known.
